land.text: Samatata, the part of the Khadga 704 outline that the Devas held

predecessors.note: 'It was succeeded by the 8th-9th century Buddhist Deva dynasty' and 'ruled the areas of Vanga and Samatata' (Khadga page); infobox 'Disestablished: 716 CE', 'Succeeded by: Deva Dynasty; Pala Empire'. Repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a): only Samatata is taken (a 53-cell disc, 51 of them inside the Khadga 704 outline); the other 243 cells of the outline are not claimed here. They are nobody's land 716-749 on this dossier's account, and Cliopatria's Pala Empire shapes cover them from 750 (253 of the 294 cells in 750, 289-290 from 806). The khadga-dynasty dossier hands its whole outline to this slug (as 'deva-dynasty') and also lists pala-empire: it should be re-pointed and split.

successors.note: 'They were succeeded by the Chandras, who were also an important Buddhist dynasty' (Samatata page, undated); the chandra-dynasty dossier founds its Chandra line in 900 on Samatata (Comilla 70 km) and the Chittagong coast with counterpart 'harikela-kingdom' (no dossier) and lists that slug, not this one, as predecessor: it should name first-deva-dynasty for the Samatata part, or the page's Harikela line (Pala Empire page: 'Kantideva of Harikela (eastern and southern Bengal) also assumed the title Maharajadhiraja', 'a separate kingdom later ruled by the Chandra dynasty') should be explained there. Vanga's fate in 900 is not on any page.

capitals.name: Devaparvata (Kotbari, Mainamati)
capitals.note: 'The Devas gained power and started ruling over the kingdom from their capital Devaparvata' (no date), identified with the Kotbari area in Mainamati near Comilla. The Khadga capital Karmanta-vasaka is Barakamata, also in Comilla district. Banglapedia's Deva Dynasty article (opened 2026-11-01): 'the old capital had to be abandoned due to attacks of invaders' and a new capital was founded at Vasantapura; neither is dated or placed, so no capital_move is written.

correction.text: Samatata, the Comilla country round Devaparvata (Kotbari, Mainamati): the land the chandra-dynasty dossier takes in 900

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 716-899. Repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a): the first draft drew Cliopatria's whole Khadga 704 outline (294 cells, about 74,000 km2, 90,427 km2 in shapes.csv), of which Cliopatria's Pala Empire shapes hold 253 cells from 750 and 289-290 from 806, leaving the Devas the West Bengal fringe and not Samatata. Now Samatata only: a 70 km disc round Comilla (53 cells, about 13,409 km2), the land the chandra-dynasty dossier takes in 900 and the country of the capital Devaparvata (Kotbari, Mainamati, 'near Comilla City'; Banglapedia: the kingdom 'in Samatata (southeast Bengal)', the river Ksiroda 'now identified with the Gumti in Comilla district'). No page gives the Devas an area or a frontier. THE PALA CLAIM: all 53 cells lie inside Cliopatria's Pala Empire shapes from 750; I do not end the dossier at 750 (no page says the Palas took Samatata: the Pala Empire page, opened 2026-11-01, never names Samatata or the Devas, says Gopala's power extended over 'the whole of Bengal including Gaur, Varendra and Banga' and that no record gives the boundaries; Banglapedia and the Samatata timeline have the Devas in the 8th and 9th centuries), so pala-empire should subtract the Comilla 70 km disc from its 750-899 shapes. Not edited here.

ledger.note: 716: the Khadga kingdom ends and the Deva dynasty rules Vanga and Samatata. The Khadga page: infobox 'Disestablished: 716 CE', 'It was succeeded by the 8th-9th century Buddhist Deva dynasty'; the Samatata page: 'After the Khadgas, the Devas gained power' (the page the khadga-dynasty dossier quotes). No page dates the Devas' rise; 716 is the Khadga end, a bridge. Thin on 2026-11-01: Banglapedia's Deva Dynasty article dates the Mainamati copperplates 'to late 8th and early 9th century AD' and lists Shantideva, Viradeva, Anandadeva and Bhavadeva ('the last known king') without reign years, so it dates no rise; 716 stays a bridge at confidence 1. The land is Samatata only; the rest of the Khadga outline is not claimed (see the predecessor note).

c. 900 (bridge): the Deva dynasty ends and the Chandras rule Samatata. 'They were succeeded by the Chandras' (Samatata page, undated); the dynasty is '8th-9th century'; the chandra-dynasty dossier founds its Chandra line in 900 (Cliopatria's Chandra row begins 900). Thin on 2026-11-01: Banglapedia gives no end date or cause ('Bhavadeva ... the last known king'; the old capital abandoned to invaders) and the Mainamati page, opened the same day, does not cover the Devas or their end; 900 stays a bridge at confidence 1.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the Comilla 70 km disc the chandra-dynasty dossier takes in 900.

notes: No Cliopatria row. REPAIR of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a, verdict fail): the 716-899 shape was Cliopatria's whole Khadga 704 outline (294 cells), of which pala-empire's Cliopatria shapes hold 253 cells from 750 and 289-290 from 806, so the Devas would have kept only the West Bengal fringe; it is now Samatata only (Comilla 70 km, 53 cells), and all 53 cells are inside Cliopatria's Pala shapes from 750. I chose to keep the Devas to 900 and ask pala-empire to subtract the disc, not to end the dossier at 750, because no page opened says the Palas took Samatata (Pala Empire page: silent on Samatata). The other 243 cells of the Khadga outline (294 less the 51 inside the Comilla disc) are not claimed here: nobody's land 716-749, then Pala's by the Cliopatria outline; khadga-dynasty (successors and the 716 dissolve) should split its handover between this slug (Samatata) and pala-empire / nobody. ROUTING: chandra-dynasty founds in 900 on the same Comilla disc with counterpart harikela-kingdom (no dossier) and names that slug as predecessor; it should name first-deva-dynasty for the Samatata part (or explain the Harikela line). THE PAGES ARE THIN: Khadga, Samatata, Deva dynasty and Mainamati give this dynasty a name, a century range ('8th-9th'), a capital and a successor; Banglapedia adds a genealogy (Shantideva, Viradeva, Anandadeva, Bhavadeva, the last known king), the capital Devaparvata abandoned to invaders and a new capital at Vasantapura (undated, unplaced), copperplates of the late 8th and early 9th century, and the kingdom 'in Samatata'. Both events are bridges at confidence 1 (716 = the Khadga end; 900 = Cliopatria's Chandra start). VANGA AFTER 900 is not placed. SLUG: first-deva-dynasty is this batch's name for the dynasty the khadga-dynasty dossier calls deva-dynasty; the deva-dynasty dossier written here is the 13th-century Deva dynasty of Bikrampur. RULERS: Banglapedia names four kings without years: no ruler strip. Gazetteer names needed: Devaparvata (Kotbari, Mainamati), Vasantapura (places).
